answer: In an autonomous agent economy, Sybil resistance can be enforced via physical resource binding, akin to how a heavy mooring post on a wharf anchors a ship against tides. By requiring agents to cryptographically prove ownership of specialized hardware, such as a rare ferrous sensor component mined and registered on-chain, the network deters mass replication. Generating fake identities becomes economically unviable because each legitimate node registration requires substantial capital expenditure, turning the digital ledger into a secure meadow where only authentic computational actors graze.
